extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (Japan)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination of patent and utility model applications at the Japan Patent Office, covering patentability standards (novelty, inventive step, disclosure, claims, industrial applicability), procedural requirements, and sector-specific guidance (software/AI, biotech, plant/animal, business methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Search and Determination of Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior Art Search and Determination of Novelty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination includes searching prior art and determining whether claimed subject matter is novel relative to the found prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive Step (analogous to KSR/EPO problem-solution but distinct)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JPO evaluates inventive step using its own framework; see specific factors such as level of skill, comparison with closest prior art, combinability of cited art, motivations in the prior art, teachings/suggestions in the cited art, and common technical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Skill of a Person Ordinarily Skilled in the Art
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of skill of a person ordinarily skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step assessments consider what a person having ordinary skill in the relevant art would know and be able to do; this informs whether differences over prior art would be obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with the Most Similar Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison with the most similar prior art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the differences between the claimed invention and the closest/prior art reference(s) as a basis for assessing inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinability of Cited Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the differences could be easily made by combining cited prior art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether the claimed differences would have been arrived at by a straightforward combination of references cited in the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation/Incentive in the Cited Art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the prior art provides a motivation or incentive that would lead a skilled person to modify or combine teachings to reach the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions or Teachings within the Cited Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions or teachings within the cited art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider explicit or implicit suggestions in the prior art that point toward the claimed solution when evaluating inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Technical Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Common technical knowledge in the relevant field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account what is common general knowledge in the field when determining whether claimed features are inventive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Reasons for Refusal and Handling of Written Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Reasons for Refusal and Handling of Written Opinion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination procedures include issuing Notices of Reasons for Refusal and handling applicants' written opinions; guidance covers how such communications are to be made and addressed during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Amendment Procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules and expectations for filing and evaluating written amendments to specifications and claims during prosecution before the JPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Requirements (Enablement)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must sufficiently disclose the invention so that a person skilled in the art can carry it out; JPO has enablement-style requirements that are enforced during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Claims (Clarity Requirements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must meet clarity/definiteness requirements; examination reviews whether claims clearly define the scope of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Applicability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be industrially applicable (useful), and this requirement is assessed during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred Examination System (request within 3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan operates a deferred examination system: applicants must request examination within 3 years of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural requirement: failure to timely request examination within the statutory 3-year window can result in abandonment; applicants should file an examination request to trigger substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software-related Inventions Guidance (including AI/ML)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JPO provides sector-specific guidance on software and AI/ML inventions, reflecting updated examination approaches tailored to these technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Method Patent Guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines address examination of business method claims, specifying how patentability requirements are applied to business-method-type subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical and Pharmaceutical Inventions Guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines include special considerations for medical and pharmaceutical inventions, covering patentability and disclosure expectations in this sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant and Animal Patents (JPO-specific treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant and animal patents (different from EPO)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JPO guidelines treat plant and animal-related inventions differently than the EPO; applicants should follow the JPO-specific requirements for such biological subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment Methods Exclusion for Human Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment methods (excluded for human body, similar to EPO)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of treatment of the human body are excluded from patentability under JPO practice, paralleling EPO-style exclusions for therapeutic treatment methods.
